title: Cursor MCP server fails authentication when mcp.json uses ${API_KEY} instead of ${env:API_KEY}
symptoms: An MCP server configured with ${API_KEY} in env or headers rejects its credentials
A config copied from Claude Code or another client works there but not in Cursor
envFile is ignored for a remote HTTP or SSE server
cause: Cursor resolves ${env:NAME}, ${userHome}, ${workspaceFolder}, ${workspaceFolderBasename}, and ${pathSeparator} in command, args, env, url, and headers; a bare ${NAME} is not one of its forms. envFile works only for stdio servers.
fix: Use ${env:NAME} for environment variables, export them where Cursor can read them, and pass remote server secrets through headers with interpolation instead of envFile.
